title: Removal of phosphate from River water using a new baffle plates electrochemical reactor
author: Hashim, Adeola Idowu, et al.
materials: The electrochemical experiments were initiated by connecting the Al electrodes to the corresponding terminals of the rectifier. 500 mL of freshly prepared phosphate solution of the desired concentration, was fed into the PBPR and kept circulated, using the peristaltic pump, during the course of experiment. Treatment time was started when the rectifier was switched on.

Progress of phosphate removal was monitored by collecting 0.5 mL samples from the reactor at 5-minute intervals during the course of the experiment. The collected samples were filtered with 0.45 μm filters (Sigma-Aldrich) to separate the unwanted sludge. The filtrate was then labelled and refrigerated to be tested at the end of each experiment. The residual phosphate concentration was measured, as mentioned before, using a standard phosphate cuvette test. The removal efficiency (R%) was calculated using the following equation [1,4]:(1)R%= IC-FCIC×100%where IC and FC are the initial and final concentrations of phosphate, in mg/L, respectively. Power consumption (Cpower) was calculated using the following formula [11,12]:(2)Cpower= I*V*tVol.where Cpower is the power consumption (W.h/m3), I is the applied current (A), V is the potential (V), t is the electrolysis time (hrs), and Vol. is the volume of solution (m3).

steps.title: Connect electrodes to rectifier
steps.instruction: Connect the aluminum electrodes to the appropriate terminals of the rectifier.

steps.title: Prepare and circulate phosphate solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 500 mL of freshly prepared phosphate solution at the desired concentration, feed it into the PBPR, and keep it circulating with a peristaltic pump throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Start electrolysis and timing
steps.instruction: Switch on the rectifier to begin electrolysis and start the treatment timer.

steps.title: Collect reactor samples
steps.instruction: Every 5 minutes, withdraw a 0.5 mL sample from the reactor.

steps.title: Filter and store samples
steps.instruction: Filter each 0.5 mL sample through a 0.45 µm Sigma‑Aldrich filter to remove sludge, label the filtrate, and refrigerate until analysis at the end of the experiment.

steps.title: Measure residual phosphate
steps.instruction: Determine the residual phosphate concentration in each stored filtrate using the standard phosphate cuvette test.

steps.title: Calculate removal efficiency
steps.instruction: Compute removal efficiency R % = (IC − FC) / IC × 100, where IC is the initial phosphate concentration (mg L⁻¹) and FC is the final concentration (mg L⁻¹).

steps.title: Calculate power consumption
steps.instruction: Calculate power consumption Cpower = I × V × t / Vol (W·h m⁻³), using the applied current I (A), potential V (V), electrolysis time t (h), and solution volume Vol (m³).

steps.title: Calculate electrode material loss
steps.instruction: Determine electrode material consumption Cmaterial = I × t × m × Z / F × 10⁻³ (kg), where I is current (A), t is treatment time (s), m is molar mass of Al (26.98 g mol⁻¹), Z = 3, and F = 96 487 C mol⁻¹.

description: Fig. 2, Fig. 3, Fig. 4 describe the removal of phosphate as a function of different key operational parameters. The investigated ranges of these operating parameters, Table 1, were selected according to the literature [2,3,[6], [7], [8]]. Fig. 2, Fig. 3, Fig. 4, Fig. 5 show the influence of each single operational parameter on the removal of phosphate.
